SMTO-HTTP-0048 — SMTO couldn't reach the Gateway to make web requests

GUID: 0fb24740-a774-41f7-a0a6-bd1d3d277d03
Slug: http-gateway-unavailable
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run work on a computer) didn't answer when SMTO checked it was ready for web requests. No sign-in details were sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running the Gateway is switched on and connected to the network. SMTO can't use a Gateway on a computer it can't reach.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the Gateway the task uses, and select Check connection. This shows whether SMTO can reach that Gateway right now.
  3. If it can't be reached, restart the Gateway program on its computer, or use another connected Gateway if you have one. A stopped or stuck Gateway can't answer SMTO's readiness check.
  4. Before running the task again, check on the service whether any change the task had already made went through. A dropped Gateway doesn't prove that earlier work didn't happen.

What success looks like

  • Check connection succeeds for the Gateway, and the task's web request runs.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed the Gateway. Don't assume earlier work failed just because the Gateway stopped answering.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server could not obtain native HTTP readiness from the selected Gateway's capabilities route (the request failed or timed out) and returned the unavailable fallback.

What this means

  • The controller could not obtain native HTTP readiness from the selected Gateway and returned the unavailable fallback. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The controller could not obtain native HTTP readiness from the selected Gateway and returned the unavailable fallback.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect Gateway selection, transport and readiness failure separately; the destination API was not tested by readiness.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway process and its connection to the Server (Gateway log, Settings › Setup › Gateways › Check connection), confirm its capabilities route answers within 5 seconds and advertises http_request, then reconnect it or select another Gateway.
  • Reconnect or select an available Gateway with native HTTP support.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Readiness is obtained from the intended connected Gateway and advertises native HTTP support.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
